findings.title: Migration aborts when embed_category is blank/unset
findings.body: `category_id` is computed with `execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id']`. The legacy `embed_category` default is an empty string, so for any site that never explicitly set it (or set it to a name that no longer exists) the INNER JOIN returns zero rows, `[0]` is `nil`, and `nil['id']` raises NoMethodError, aborting the migration after the table was already created. Crucially, this is exactly the scenario the following `if category_id == 0` fallback is meant to handle, but that fallback is unreachable because the exception fires first. Guard the result before casting (e.g. `(...[0].try(:[], 'id') || 0).to_i`); the same unsafe pattern exists for the `uncategorized_category_id` lookup on line 15.

findings.title: Host value interpolated directly into raw SQL
findings.body: The INSERT does `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (...) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)"`, interpolating the legacy host string `h` straight into the statement. If any stored value contains a single quote (or other SQL metacharacters) the statement becomes malformed and the migration fails; since the source is admin-controlled setting data, it is also an injection vector. Use a parameterized insert or model creation/`quote` instead of string interpolation.

findings.title: Legacy host entries copied without normalizing scheme/path
findings.body: The old `embeddable_hosts` setting allowed entries with a scheme and path (e.g. `http://eviltrout.com`, `https://example.com/1234`, as used by the old specs), and they are copied verbatim into the new `host` column. But `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` compares `lower(host)` against the bare `URI#host` (`eviltrout.com`), so a stored `http://eviltrout.com` never matches. After upgrade, every site that configured hosts with a scheme/path has all embeds rejected with `invalid referer host`. Normalize each value (strip scheme and path, as the model's `before_validation` does) during migration.

findings.title: Host matching is case-sensitive for the caller's host
findings.body: `record_for_host` runs `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` but passes the raw `URI#host`, which preserves case. Because only the column is lowercased, a referer whose hostname contains any uppercase letter (e.g. `Example.com`) will not match the stored `example.com`, so `host_allowed?` returns false and embedding is incorrectly blocked. Downcase the parameter (`host.downcase`) to match the column lowering.

findings.title: before_validation crashes on nil host
findings.body: `before_validation` calls `self.host.sub!(...)` without a nil guard. If a record is saved with a blank/missing `host` (e.g. the admin form posts no host, or `EmbeddableHost.new` is persisted), `nil.sub!` raises NoMethodError and the request returns 500 instead of a normal validation failure. Use `self.host = self.host.to_s...` or guard with `if self.host`.

findings.title: update/destroy raise 500 on unknown id instead of 404
findings.body: `update` and `destroy` do `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then call `save_host(host)` / `host.destroy` with no nil check. A request for a non-existent id raises NoMethodError on `nil` and returns 500 rather than 404. `save_host` also assumes `params[:embeddable_host]` is present, so a malformed payload crashes the same way.

findings.title: Embedded hosts missing from response root; UI list will be empty
findings.body: `has_many :embeddable_hosts, ..., embed: :ids` emits only the `embeddable_host_ids` array on the `embedding` object; it does not put the `embeddable_hosts` collection in the response root unless `include: true` is set. The JS store's `_hydrateEmbedded` (mirrored by the `create-pretender` fixtures, which return both `*_ids` fields and root collections) needs `root['embeddable_hosts']` to rebuild the records; without it `embedding.embeddable_hosts` hydrates to an empty (or undefined-filled) array, so the admin Embedding page shows no hosts. Add `include: true`.

findings.title: Fabricator files were swapped
findings.body: `category_fabricator.rb` now defines the `:embeddable_host` fabricator, while `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains all the category fabricators (`:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category`, `:private_category`). It only works because every file under `spec/fabricators` is loaded, but the filenames no longer describe their contents and will confuse future edits. Move each fabricator back into the matching file.

findings.title: New admin controllers only tested for inheritance
findings.body: Both `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` and `Admin::EmbeddingController` specs only assert that the class subclasses `Admin::AdminController`; none of `create`/`update`/`destroy` (including not-found ids and blank host input) is exercised. This is why the 500-causing nil handling in `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` is not caught. Add request specs for the happy path and the not-found/invalid-input paths.

findings.title: Test name no longer matches what it verifies
findings.body: `topic.rb` removed the `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts` check from `expandable_first_post?`, but this test still claims to cover the 'embeddable_host is blank' case. It now passes only because `embed_truncate` defaults to false and `has_topic_embed?` is stubbed false, so it would not catch a regression in the embed gating (there is no longer any such gate). Rename or rewrite the test to assert the actual conditions.
